comment: Hand-maintained parameter types for tools/gen-natives.cs: native id -> parameter name -> "Type" or "Type newName", and "result": "bool" for a predicate (its doc says 1 or 0, a flag, a check) whose int result the shipped scripts use only as a condition (Common.PadIsPressedRaw and Btl.ActorPartnerReady nearly only; their few value uses read AsInt(...)). The types are the enums of src/Ffx.Atel.Game/Enums.g.cs (tools/gen-enums.cs), Map (Map.g.cs, tools/gen-maps.cs), Sfx and TextId (a message of the script's table, written Text[n]); "int:Battle" is an int whose values the constants of a static class name (Battle.g.cs), for a parameter or a result (Atel.Values). Sources: each native's doc (data/natives.json, from ffx-rust symbols/ffx.sym) names the argument (actor selector, property, command, motion, msg); the property ids are MsGetChrStatInfo's (ffx-rust docs/formats/battle.md). The "docs" section: per native a modder-facing "summary" (and optionally a verified "name", "rename" of parameters and "params" descriptions), written from what is verified (ffx-rust symbols/ffx.sym without its '?' guesses, the ported natives in ffx-rust crates/ffx-script/src/vm/bridge/, the Ghidra dump); the symbol's notes then go to <remarks>. tools/gen-natives.cs fails on names that mislead ("Ret").

0x5057.name: SetBoneUpdateOf
0x5057.summary: <see cref="SetBoneUpdate"/> for another worker's model (<c>Ch_SetCalcNorm</c> on it). Returns what that returns, 0 when the worker has no model.

params.worker: The worker whose model it sets.

0x5057.notes: handler 0x00a78af0 pops on, then worker; AtelGetBasicWork(worker) (0x0086a830), its character (AtelGetCharHandle, 0x0086ae80), then Ch_SetCalcNorm(chr, on) (0x00835750), the call 0x5056 makes on the worker's own model.

0x01ba.name: ChrGetEquipModelOf
0x01ba.summary: <see cref="ChrGetEquipModel"/> for another worker: the armor model (<paramref name="kind"/> 1) or weapon model (0) of the party member that worker is bound to; 0 when it is bound to none.
0x01ba.notes: handler 0x0085beb0 pops kind, then worker, clamps kind to 0-1; AtelGetBasicWork(worker) +0x40 (the bound character) 0-7: AtelGetElemId(chr, kind) (0x0086b150: MsGetSaveChrArmorModel for 1, else MsGetSaveChrWeaponModel), else 0. 0x0119 does the same with the worker's own +0x40.

0x019d.name: WorkerDetachAndDispose
0x019d.summary: Releases what the worker is attached to, as <see cref="WorkerDetach"/>; with <paramref name="dispose"/> non-zero it also frees an attached model's character data (<c>ChN_DataDispose</c>).

params.dispose: Non-zero to free the model's data too (the scripts pass 1).

0x019d.notes: handler Worker_Detach (0x0085ca00) pops dispose; by the attachment kind (+0xaa): 1 a model: AtelBindElemOff for elements 0 and 1, TkCh_Dispose(+0x9c), and with dispose ChN_DataDispose(+0xa8, 0) (0x00824f00); 2 MsBindOffCamera; 4/5 AtelSetBindObject; then +0xaa = 0, +0xa8 = 0. WorkerDetach (0x0005, 0x0085cdc0) pushes 0 and jumps into this handler. 730 of the 764 calls pass 1.

0x019c.summary: Returns 1. Every call in the shipped scripts is the last term of a button check (<c>MsgIsReady(0) == 1 & AsBool(PadPressed() & 32) & AlwaysTrue019c()</c>); on PC the term is always true.
0x019c.notes: handler 0x00856630 is mov eax, 1; ret (no pops). The 961 calls: PadPressed() & 32 (881, 379 of them after MsgIsReady(0) == 1) and & 160 (80, after MsgIsReady). What the PS2 version tested there is not known: neither ffx.sym, Fahrenheit (AtelFn_Std_19C_RetI) nor a PS2 executable says, so it keeps its name.

0x501b.summary: The same as <see cref="SetMotion"/> (<c>0x5000</c>): sets the worker's model to motion <paramref name="motion"/>. Returns 0.
0x501b.notes: handlers 0x00a792d0 and 0x00a78770 are the same code: AtelPopStackInteger, AtelGetCharHandle, Ch_SetSequence(chr, motion) (0x00837ac0), 0.

0x501e.summary: Waits until the worker's model has finished its motion, as <see cref="WaitMotion"/>; in the game's debug mode it also counts the frames it waited.
0x501e.notes: poll 0x00a793c0 ends (5) when chr +0x736 is 0, as WaitMotion's (0x5003, 0x00a788a0); with g_DebugMode (0x012fb80c) 1 it counts frames in 0x022fb4d8. Its start slot is a bare ret.

0x5021.summary: The same as <see cref="SetMotionSpeed"/> (<c>0x5018</c>): sets the speed of the worker's model's motion. Returns 0.
0x5021.notes: handlers 0x00a79510 and 0x00a791e0 are the same code: Ch_SetMotionSpeed(chr, speed) (0x0082b380), 0.

0x6006.name: EyeAimAtXZ
0x6006.summary: Aims the camera's eye in polar form at a point: yaw towards (x, z) from the side's base, pitch = pitch + distance / pitchDivisor, length = length + distance / lengthDivisor.
0x6006.notes: handler calls MsAtelCameraEyeAddArea_007bb410(worker, args, stack, side 1, short -1) (ffx.sym; despite the name it sets no area): six floats popped, the pitch from degrees; kind 4 (MsCameraSetAimPolar_007bf330): yaw towards (x, z) from the side's base, pitch = pitch + distance / pitchDivisor, length = length + distance / lengthDivisor (ffx-rust crates/ffx-battle/src/camera.rs and camera_native.rs (ported, checked against the game)).

0x6007.name: EyeAimAt
0x6007.summary: Aims the camera's eye in polar form at a point: yaw towards (x, y, z), keeping the point's own pitch (plus distance / pitchDivisor), length = length + distance / lengthDivisor.
0x6007.notes: handler calls MsAtelCameraEyeAddArea_007bb410(worker, args, stack, side 1, short 0) (ffx.sym; despite the name it sets no area): six floats popped, the pitch from degrees; kind 5 (MsCameraSetAimPolar2_007bf420, short 0): yaw towards (x, y, z), keeping the point's own pitch (plus distance / pitchDivisor), length = length + distance / lengthDivisor (ffx-rust crates/ffx-battle/src/camera.rs and camera_native.rs (ported, checked against the game)).

0x6008.name: EyeAimShortOf
0x6008.summary: Aims the camera's eye in polar form at a point: as kind 5, but the length is the distance less (length + distance / lengthDivisor): it stops short of the point.
0x6008.notes: handler calls MsAtelCameraEyeAddArea_007bb410(worker, args, stack, side 1, short 1) (ffx.sym; despite the name it sets no area): six floats popped, the pitch from degrees; kind 6 (MsCameraSetAimPolar2_007bf420, short 1): as kind 5, but the length is the distance less (length + distance / lengthDivisor): it stops short of the point (ffx-rust crates/ffx-battle/src/camera.rs and camera_native.rs (ported, checked against the game)).

0x6024.name: FocusAimAtXZ
0x6024.summary: Aims the camera's focus point in polar form at a point: yaw towards (x, z) from the side's base, pitch = pitch + distance / pitchDivisor, length = length + distance / lengthDivisor.
0x6024.notes: handler calls MsAtelCameraEyeAddArea_007bb410(worker, args, stack, side 0, short -1) (ffx.sym; despite the name it sets no area): six floats popped, the pitch from degrees; kind 4 (MsCameraSetAimPolar_007bf330): yaw towards (x, z) from the side's base, pitch = pitch + distance / pitchDivisor, length = length + distance / lengthDivisor (ffx-rust crates/ffx-battle/src/camera.rs and camera_native.rs (ported, checked against the game)).

0x6025.name: FocusAimAt
0x6025.summary: Aims the camera's focus point in polar form at a point: yaw towards (x, y, z), keeping the point's own pitch (plus distance / pitchDivisor), length = length + distance / lengthDivisor.
0x6025.notes: handler calls MsAtelCameraEyeAddArea_007bb410(worker, args, stack, side 0, short 0) (ffx.sym; despite the name it sets no area): six floats popped, the pitch from degrees; kind 5 (MsCameraSetAimPolar2_007bf420, short 0): yaw towards (x, y, z), keeping the point's own pitch (plus distance / pitchDivisor), length = length + distance / lengthDivisor (ffx-rust crates/ffx-battle/src/camera.rs and camera_native.rs (ported, checked against the game)).

0x6026.name: FocusAimShortOf
0x6026.summary: Aims the camera's focus point in polar form at a point: as kind 5, but the length is the distance less (length + distance / lengthDivisor): it stops short of the point.
0x6026.notes: handler calls MsAtelCameraEyeAddArea_007bb410(worker, args, stack, side 0, short 1) (ffx.sym; despite the name it sets no area): six floats popped, the pitch from degrees; kind 6 (MsCameraSetAimPolar2_007bf420, short 1): as kind 5, but the length is the distance less (length + distance / lengthDivisor): it stops short of the point (ffx-rust crates/ffx-battle/src/camera.rs and camera_native.rs (ported, checked against the game)).

0x6005.name: AddPolar
0x6005.summary: Adds to the eye's polar placement around the point it looks at (<see cref="SetPolar"/>): angles in degrees and a distance.
0x6005.notes: handler 0x007b9320: MsAtelCameraPolar_007bb5d0(worker, args, stack, side 1, add -1), which pops the distance and the two angles (degrees to radians) into Cam_AddPolar (Cam_SetPolar for add 0, native 0x6004); the eye twin of RefAddPolar (0x6023).

0x600f.name: EyeClearAreas
0x600f.summary: Removes the eye's areas (the line, circle and path limits added by <see cref="AddLineArea"/> and the like).
0x600f.notes: handler 0x007b9520: MsCameraResetFilter(cam, 1) (Fahrenheit's name, from the Switch build): the eye channel's filter count +4 = 0; the eye twin of RefClearAreas (0x602d, side 0).

0x6011.name: EyeMoveFrameLinear
0x6011.summary: Starts the eye's move to its target over <paramref name="frames"/> frames, linear, with move mode 1 (<see cref="Move"/> is mode 0).
0x6011.notes: handler 0x007b9730: MsCameraMoveFrame(cam, side 1, mode 1, frames, curve 1); curve 1 is linear, 3 a cosine ease (MsCameraMoveCalc, ffx-rust camera.rs). Move (0x6010) is (1, 0, frames, 1), EyeMoveFrame (0x6013) (1, 1, frames, 3). What mode 1 changes (the move's byte +1) is not known.

0x6012.name: MoveCosine
0x6012.summary: Starts the eye's move to its target over <paramref name="frames"/> frames with a cosine ease (<see cref="Move"/> is linear).
0x6012.notes: handler 0x007b9800: MsCameraMoveFrame(cam, side 1, mode 0, frames, curve 3); curve 3 is a cosine ease (MsCameraMoveCalc, ffx-rust camera.rs); Move (0x6010) passes curve 1.

0x6030.name: FocusTimeCosine
0x6030.summary: Starts the focus point's move to its target over <paramref name="frames"/> frames with a cosine ease (<see cref="FocusTimeLinear"/> is linear).
0x6030.notes: handler 0x007b8050: MsCameraMoveFrame(cam, side 0, mode 0, frames, curve 3); FocusTimeLinear (0x602e) is (0, 0, frames, 1).

0x6017.name: EyeMoveDivide
0x6017.summary: Sets the four move-divide values of the camera's eye (<c>MsCameraMoveDivide</c>). What they divide is not known yet.
0x6017.notes: handler: MsAtelCameraMoveDivide_007bb520(worker, args, stack, side 1): four floats popped into MsCameraMoveDivide(cam, side, ...) (Fahrenheit's name), the channel's +0x70..+0x7c (ffx-rust crates/ffx-battle/src/camera.rs and camera_native.rs (ported, checked against the game)).

0x6035.name: RefMoveDivide
0x6035.summary: Sets the four move-divide values of the camera's focus point (<c>MsCameraMoveDivide</c>). What they divide is not known yet.
0x6035.notes: handler: MsAtelCameraMoveDivide_007bb520(worker, args, stack, side 0): four floats popped into MsCameraMoveDivide(cam, side, ...) (Fahrenheit's name), the channel's +0x70..+0x7c (ffx-rust crates/ffx-battle/src/camera.rs and camera_native.rs (ported, checked against the game)).

0x6019.name: EyeResetDir
0x6019.summary: Turns off the eye's direction vector (set by <see cref="SetDir"/>).
0x6019.notes: handler 0x007b9ac0: MsCameraResetDirVector(cam, 1) (Fahrenheit's name): the side's +0x33 flag off, its +0x70 vector zero; the eye twin of RefResetDir (0x6037).

0x601c.name: SetFocusList1
0x601c.summary: <see cref="SetFocusList"/> with flag 1: the eye follows the focus list in <paramref name="list"/>.
0x601c.notes: handler 0x007b8330: MsCameraSetFocusList_007bf520(cam, side 1, flags 1, &list, degrees in radians): a request of kind 8 with the list and the angle; SetFocusList (0x601e) passes flags 0. What the flag (ORed into the request's +3) changes is not known.

0x601d.name: SetTargetPolar1
0x601d.summary: Makes the eye follow <paramref name="target"/> in polar form (request kind 9), with flag 1.
0x601d.notes: handler 0x007b8470: MsCameraSetTargetPolar_007bf600(cam, side 1, flags 1, &target, radians, y, x) (ffx-rust ffx-sg camera.rs): kind 9 following the target, the angle added to the polar form's +0x100 on the running request. SetTargetPolar (0x601f) passes flags 0.

0x601f.name: SetTargetPolar
0x601f.summary: Makes the eye follow <paramref name="target"/> in polar form (request kind 9).
0x601f.notes: handler 0x007b8530: as 0x601d with flags 0: MsCameraSetTargetPolar_007bf600(cam, side 1, 0, &target, radians, y, x).

0x6021.name: RefGetPos
0x6021.summary: Stores the point the camera looks at in three variables (<see cref="GetPos"/> is the eye's).
0x6021.notes: handler 0x007b9d40: Atel_CamGetVars_007ba3c0(worker, args, stack, side 0): three variable addresses popped, Cam_GetPos(cam, 0, &x, &y, &z); GetPos (0x6003) is side 1.

0x6028.name: RefLineFilter
0x6028.summary: Adds a line limit of kind 0 to the focus point: the segment from (<paramref name="x1"/>, <paramref name="z1"/>) to (<paramref name="x2"/>, <paramref name="z2"/>) with width <paramref name="r"/> (<see cref="LineFilter"/> is the eye's).
0x6028.notes: handler 0x007ba0e0: MsAtelCameraLineFilter_007bb2b0(worker, args, stack, side 0, kind 0) -> MsCameraAddLineFilter_007bf0b0: one more filter record (at most five) with the segment in the xz plane, record type 0 (2 for a non-zero kind, RefAddLineArea) (ffx-rust crates/ffx-battle/src/camera.rs and camera_native.rs (ported, checked against the game)).

0x603c.name: SetYaw
0x603c.summary: Places the eye in polar form (request kind 10): yaw and pitch in degrees, and a length.
0x603c.notes: handler 0x007b9400: MsAtelCameraYaw_007bac40(worker, args, stack, side 1): four floats popped, the first two pushed from degrees, into MsCameraSetAtelYaw_007befc0(cam, 1, yaw, pitch, length), which stores +0x40, +0x44, +0x48 with kind 10 and leaves the fourth value unused (dump); the eye twin of RefSetYaw (0x603d).

0x603f.name: FocusOnActors
0x603f.summary: Points the focus point at the battle actors <paramref name="actorA"/> and <paramref name="actorB"/> (their mean camera position), lowered by <paramref name="lift"/>% of their height.
0x603f.notes: handler 0x007b86f0: MsAtelCameraSetBtl_007bad10(worker, args, stack, side 0) -> MsCameraSetBtl(cam, 0, actor, mode 0, a, b, lift / 100, 0, 0, 0): channel kind 0xb; MsCamSetBtl averages MsGetChrInfo kind 9 (camera position) of the two sets, y less lift times the height (kind 10) (ffx-rust crates/ffx-battle/src/camera.rs and camera_native.rs (ported, checked against the game)). The twin of SetBtl (0x603e, side 1).

0x6043.name: EyeMoveStat
0x6043.summary: Sets the eye's move-stat byte (<c>MsCameraMoveStat</c>, the value inverted).
0x6043.notes: handler 0x007b8660: MsCameraMoveStat(cam, 1, v ^ 0xffff) (Fahrenheit's name): the channel's +7 = v; the eye twin of RefMoveStat (0x6042). +7 holds the lane flags a move leaves alone (MsCameraMoveAcc), so the value says which axes move.

0x6046.notes: handler: MsAtelCameraSpline_007bb970(worker, args, stack, side 1): flags, speed, t and the spline popped into MsCameraSetSpline(cam, side, spline, t, speed, flags) (Fahrenheit's name); 0 and 1 are the built-in splines at 0x01136b68 (used from 3 points on), else AtelGetRealVarAdrs (ffx-rust crates/ffx-battle/src/camera.rs and camera_native.rs (ported, checked against the game)).

0x002a.name: TurnSetRoll
0x002a.summary: Sets the roll the worker turns to (see <see cref="TurnStart"/>), in radians; returns it wrapped into one turn.
0x002a.notes: handler 0x00859bb0: the angle wrapped into the turn block's +0x28 and the wrapped rest from the position's +0x38 into +0x34, as 0x0029 does for +0x30 and 0x0028 for the yaw +0x34. Axis convention: the position block's rotation is +0x30 pitch, +0x34 yaw, +0x38 roll (ffx-rust docs/formats/script.md, Atel_TurnUpdate_00869510). Checked for Atel#: +0x34 is the heading (Native_SetYaw writes it with the move heading +0x20, Ch_SetRot is the model's yaw), and the scripts set +0x30 from the vertical angle to a target: Turn.Pitch = Move.PitchToTarget 2,206 times (0x0020, the pitch of Math_YawPitchTo, 0x0088b4d0), so +0x30 is pitch and +0x38, the third axis, is roll.
